blocks.text: Mrs Hocknell, we'd got to 448, please. I think we had just dealt with that particular tile, which is the giving of an adrenaline bolus recorded by [Dr A].
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So if we move on, please, at 449 to Lucy Letby's nursing note timed at 12.47. If we could just click on that, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's her record of the same event; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 450, please, we've got the record on the computer, signed and countersigned by Dr Burke and Lucy Letby.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 451, that same information recorded on the resuscitation record.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 452, the scribe wrote -- and if we just have a look at this, please, at the original, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So this is a running record. As we can see, that started with CPR at 9.50 that morning. If we scroll down, please, Mr Murphy, we can see that we're dealing at this stage with the CPR that started at 12.28.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And we're dealing at this specific point with the adrenaline number 5 at 12.50, where it also says, "CPR stopped".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we scroll up the page again, please. We can see CPR at 09.50, followed by -- which then restored spontaneous calculation. We see CPR at 11.30 and this is the third set of CPR on this specific day, which is Friday, 24 June.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So that's tile 452. Continuing with the sequence, at tile 453, [Dr A]'s record of an adrenaline bolus being given.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed at 454 by Dr Burke and Nurse Lucy Letby recording the administration of a bolus of 20ml of sodium chloride.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That is also recorded by the scribe in that note that we just looked at at tile 455?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And in the clinical notes at 456, by [Dr A]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: ROSC, if we click on this because it came up on Friday, I now know the answer, was an abbreviation that I don't think we had worked out on Friday. "Restoration of spontaneous circulation", I think, is what it stands for.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 457 next, please, the resuscitation record records the recommencement of compressions.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And this is then a WhatsApp message from [Nurse E] to Lucy Letby at the same time at 458?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That reads:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Hope you're having [an] okay day."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So back to the carousel, please, and at 459 [Dr A] recorded the administration of sodium bicarbonate, which is recorded in the IV and subcutaneous infusion prescription chart at 460 by Dr Burke.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 461, there is also a record of that, or a bolus of that, noted by Dr Burke and Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And also on the resuscitation record at 462?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 463, [Dr A], at 12.55, records a second fluid bolus of 12ml per kilo?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And at 464 we have the observation chart at 13.00 hours, together with the intensive care chart and the fluid requirement at 465 at the same time.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. At 466, also at 13.00 hours, do we have the neonatal unit intensive care chart equipment settings with data recorded by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we just, just to sort of recalibrate ourselves, look at that please, and get the original.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Here we have 13.00 hours and we can see a number of readings recorded. And if we go all the way to the bottom we can see Lucy Letby's initials against those three columns which are timed at 13.14 and 15.00 hours respectively.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 467, please, do we have [Dr B]'s notes concerning a conversation that she had with Dr Rackham, the transport consultant from Arrowe Park?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And at 468, at 13.03 hours, some door swipe entry data for [Dr B] coming into the neonatal entrance?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed by the same record, 2 minutes later, at 13.05, tile 469?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And also the same door being passed through by Lucy Letby at 13.05, tile 470?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 471, at the same time, 13.05, is there a note of dobutamine being administered to [Baby P], signed by Dr Cooke and countersigned by both Lucy Letby and Christopher Booth?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed at 472 by further door swipe data for Lucy Letby, timed at 13.06?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 473, timed at 13.10, Lucy Letby's nursing note, which, as with all the other nursing notes, she made much later that evening at 21.18?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we just look at that, please. That records that dobutamine was commenced, inotropes running via peripheral line in right arm?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 474, timed at 13.10, do we have that dobutamine recorded by the scribe --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- on those rough notes, as we do at 475?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: But at 475 we also have a heart rate and other measurements recorded?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 476 at 13.10, do we have [Dr A]'s note of the dobutamine being commenced?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 477, [Dr B]'s notes concerning this particular resuscitation and the administration of dopamine and dobutamine?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 478 do we have door swipe data for Angela McShane, followed at 479 by door swipe data for Dr Brearey?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 480 is an infusion prescription for sodium chloride, signed off by Dr Burke and Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 481 in the nursing notes, Lucy Letby has made a note of that sodium bicarbonate. If we just look at that, please. It says:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Sodium bicarbonate infusion commenced via second peripheral line in left hand."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So that appears to establish that there are two peripheral lines running into [Baby P].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 482, at 13.25, did the scribe record the administration of sodium bicarbonate?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 483, also at 13.25 hours, Lucy Letby made a further nursing note. If we go to that, please. Does that record:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Hydrocortisone given via IO line along with metronidazole at 13.25"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did you say via the IO line?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I thought I did.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's a different means of access. It's intraosseous, with which we're now familiar.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 484 there is a further note made by Lucy Letby.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we can go to this, please. Does that record:
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Some drugs via peripheral line, some via IO access"?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: So precisely the point his Lordship has just made and then:
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Morphine discontinued as nil access to run. 10% stopped as [Baby P] receiving over fluid requirements through infusions. Right arm with inotropes in noted [maybe that should be 'is noted'] to be swelling and digits purple. Trace blood obtained from NG tube. [Baby P] pale."
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: So that again is a note made at 21.18; is that right?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 485, is there some door entry data for Dr Burke?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 486, a further door entry for Dr Burke?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then the scribe, at 487 and 488, records the administration of the infusion of bicarbonate?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Together with the same information recorded by [Dr A]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we go to -- sorry, then at 489 through to 491, door swipe data between 13.27 and 13.30 for Dr Burke and [Dr B].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Whilst all that's going on, at 492 do we have a text or a WhatsApp message sent by Lucy Letby to [Nurse E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Just to remind ourselves, [Nurse E] had sent Lucy Letby a message a few minutes earlier; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Hope you having okay day."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is 13.30, so 40 minutes later. What did Lucy Letby send to [Nurse E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Another triplet collapsed."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Is that followed almost immediately, at 493, by [Nurse E] replying:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "What? Is it okay?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Do we then have four sets of door swipe data, a pair for Nurse Angela McShane and a pair for [Dr B]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: They are timed at 13.31 through to 13.36. At tile 498, timed at 13.38, are there some blood gas results for [Baby P]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed by, at 499, at the same time, a manuscript record of those results made in the gas chart by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Again, we'll deal with these with the medics in due course, but also at the same time, tile 500, do we have notes made by [Dr A] recording some of these gas results?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 501, timed at 13.41 and 26 seconds, did Lucy Letby respond to [Nurse E]'s question, "What?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is it okay?" with a message?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied, "No, resus".
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: 502, door swipe data for Angela McShane and then [Nurse E]'s response to that message coming about 5 minutes later saying:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "You looking after them? Okay since resus?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then door swipe data for Dr Ukoh at 504, timed at 13.58?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed by 14.00 hours by three tiles, 505 through to 507, recording [Baby P]'s vital signs, the fluid requirements and administration, what was being administered, and also the intensive care chart data, all manually recorded by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. At 508 and 509, is there door swipe data for both Dr Burke and Lucy Letby at 14.06 and 14.11 hours respectively?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed by a figure recorded by the scribe at 14.15 at tile 510, which simply reads, "68??" and then "(52)"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At tile 511 is there door swipe data for [Nurse D] coming into the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed, at tile 512, by some blood results recorded by [Dr B]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 513 a note made by a pharmacist, Alice Rafferty, concerning the administration of pancuronium?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 514 did Dr Burke and Lucy Letby record at 14.30 the administration of Curosurf, a surfactant?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 515, also at 14.30, [Dr A] recorded the administration of hydrocortisone?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 516, at the same time, in her retrospective nursing notes did Lucy Letby make a note concerning the administration of surfactant?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And can you just tell us what she wrote, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "240 milligrams surfactant given. Stable on ventilator. Blood gases as charted."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. At 517, 518 and 519 are there further notes made by [Dr A] and the scribe relating to the administration of metronidazole, hydrocortisone and Curosurf?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then some door swipe data at tile 520, timed at 14.31, for Dr Brearey?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then the WhatsApp conversation recommences at tile 521 with a message from Lucy Letby to [Nurse E], timed at 14.31?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I've got him. Everybody involved. They unwell. Waiting for transport."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 522 did [Nurse E] respond, "Bloody hell", followed by a social message at tile 523?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We then have door swipe data for [Dr B] at tile 524 timed at 14.45, but the WhatsApp conversation continued at 525 with a message from Lucy Letby to [Nurse E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Meant very unwell. Just grabbing quick drink. Got 2 IO access and chest drain. Gases are appalling. On triple inotropes. Not sure where we go from else."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That's corrected in the next text, I think, to "here", "Where we go from here".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And then at 527 there was some social messaging from Lucy Letby to [Nurse E] at about -- I think it's actually about 7 seconds after that other message.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 528, door swipe data recording the reappearance of Dr Brearey?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then Lucy Letby sent some emojis, which probably speak for themselves --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- to [Dr A] at 14.55?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We then have, at 530 through to 533, between the hours of 14.56 and 14.59, door swipe data relating to [Dr B] and to Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Just putting the door swipe data into the context of the messages sent to [Dr A] and to [Nurse E], there have been three messages sent at 14.48 by Lucy Letby to [Nurse E], those emojis at 14.55 by Lucy Letby to [Dr A], and then Lucy Letby
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: comes into the unit at tile 533 at 14.59, in other words, 4 minutes after those two emojis that she'd sent to [Dr A]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At tile 534 were [Baby P]'s vital signs noted on the chart, timed at 15.00, by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did Lucy Letby then, at 535, make a note in the nursing notes?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Can you tell us what she recorded, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Pigtail chest drain inserted by Registrar [Dr A]."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 536, also timed at 15.00 hours, did Lucy Letby record various data in the fluid requirements/intensive care chart?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Together with other information in the equipment settings chart at tile 537?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 538 did the door swipe data record the arrival or re-arrival of [Dr B] back into the NNU entrance doors?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 539 do we have [Dr A]'s notes, also timed at 15.00 hours, concerning his insertion of the pigtail chest drain --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- which the jury may recall is actually shown in one of the radiographs that we saw on Friday?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did [Dr B] at 15.00 hours, tile 540, record the arrival of Dr Rackham with the transport team?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 541 through to 543, is there door swipe data covering the period 15.06 to 15.10 relating to Dr Brearey?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: You have then put a tile in at 544 recording a further event related to [Baby P]; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That's followed at 545 by [Dr A]'s notes recording:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Cardiorespiratory arrest, CPR commenced, 15.14."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That time is replicated by the scribe at tile 546; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We'll look at that, please. Up at the top, please, Mr Murphy. 15.14, "CPR" is underlined. We then have what we now recognise as a fairly predictable sequence of the administration of adrenaline and bicarbonate and other drugs, which are timed in steps.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 547, did the door swipe data record Christopher Booth passing through the entrance doors at 15.14?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 548, 15.15, did Lucy Letby make a note concerning the arrival of the transport team?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Go to that and you can tell us what she wrote, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Transport team arrived. Consultant [Dr B] had liaised with them during the day. Further collapse shortly after arrival. Resuscitation as documented in medical notes."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Do we then have a sequence of tiles, from 549 onwards, recording the administration of adrenaline, sodium bicarbonate and phenobarbitone?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At tile 570 we have door swipe data for Angela McShane?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 571, the litany of drugs being given to [Baby P] recommences at 15.35. So that's tiles 571 and 572. At 573, what's recorded as -- if we look at 573, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We will be hearing from [Dr A] in a moment, but a relatively -a sort of entry we've not seen before here:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "High dose adrenaline, 0.6ml."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Followed by the X-ray report at 574, which we saw with Dr Arthurs, Professor Arthurs, on Friday. Then the litany of resuscitation drugs recommences at 575 with adrenaline and at 576, 577.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Some door swipe data for [Nurse D] at 578, but the drugs again at 579, 580 and 581.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We then come to [Nurse E]'s response to Lucy Letby's message that she'd sent a short while earlier. The substantial message read:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Meant very unwell. Just grabbing quick drink. Got 2 IO access and chest drain. Gasses are appalling, on triple inotropes. Not sure where we go from here."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And [Nurse E] responded at 582:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Oh how sad! What about the third?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then door swipe entry at 583 and 584 for Dr Brearey and [Nurse D].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Meanwhile, the resuscitation drugs were still being administered. Atropine at 585 and 586, noted by Lucy Letby at 587.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Also noted by Dr Burke at 588?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Together with sodium bicarbonate at 589?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Replicated by the scribe at 590.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 591 and 592, the seventh dose of adrenaline.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed by, at 593, [Dr A]'s notes that he will take us through when he gives evidence when you have finished. Then Lucy Letby's notes timed at 16.00 hours, tile 594, recording the administration of dopamine, dobutamine, adrenaline and bicarbonate.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did the scribe then at 595 also at 16.00 simply write "Stop"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON
